title: Check yourself: type casting and conversion

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A `short` field `slots` holds 32,000. A scheduler runs `slots += 1_000;`, where 1_000 is an `int` literal. What happens?

options.text: It fails at compile time, since `short` plus `int` gives an `int` that needs an explicit cast
options.says: a compound assignment includes a cast back to the left-hand type, so it compiles

options.text: It fails at run time, since the sum 33,000 is above the largest value a `short` holds
options.says: no primitive cast checks the range; nothing throws

options.text: It stores a negative number, since `+=` casts the sum back to `short`, keeping its low 16 bits
options.says: `a += b` means `a = (short) (a + b)`, and the narrowing keeps the low bits: 33,000 - 65,536 = -32,536

options.text: It stores Short.MAX_VALUE, since `+=` casts the sum back to `short`, clamping it to the range
options.says: only casts from floating point clamp; integer narrowing keeps the low bits

origin.section: A Narrowing Integer Cast Keeps the Low Bits and Never Fails

questions.stem: A rate limiter computes `int allowed = (int) (creditEuros / costPerCallEuros);` with two `double`s. A tenant is misconfigured with a cost per call of 0.0 and has 50.0 euros of credit. What is `allowed`?

options.text: Integer.MAX_VALUE, since the quotient is Infinity and the cast clamps it
options.says: 50.0 / 0.0 is Infinity, and a cast from floating point clamps values above the range to MAX_VALUE

options.text: 0, since the quotient is NaN and the cast turns NaN into 0
options.says: a positive number divided by 0.0 is Infinity; 0.0 / 0.0 is NaN (unit 1.1.1)

options.text: No value, since dividing by 0.0 throws ArithmeticException before the cast runs
options.says: floating-point division by zero returns Infinity or NaN; only integer division throws

options.text: A negative number, since the quotient is Infinity and the cast keeps its low bits
options.says: a cast from floating point clamps instead of keeping low bits

origin.section: Casting a double to int or long Truncates Toward Zero, Clamps at the Range, and Turns NaN Into 0

questions.stem: A consumer reports its last processed sequence number, a `long`, through `gauge(String name, double value)`, and the replay job reads it back with `(long) value`. Today's sequence number is 18,014,398,509,481,985. What does the replay job get?

options.text: The same number, since the conversion to `double` is implicit and needs no cast
options.says: needing no cast doesn't make a conversion exact: long to double is widening and can round above 2^53

options.text: A different number, since a `double` this large is clamped when cast back to `long`
options.says: the value is far below Long.MAX_VALUE; a cast from floating point clamps only values outside the range

options.text: The same number, since a `double` has a wider range than a `long`
options.says: a double's range is wider, but it has 53 significant bits to a 64-bit long's, so a long above 2^53 can be rounded

options.text: A different number, since a `double` has fewer significant bits than a `long`
options.says: a double has 53 significant bits, so a long above 2^53 can be rounded: 18,014,398,509,481,985 (2^54 + 1) comes back as 2^54

origin.section: Widening to float or double Is Implicit and Rounds Large Values

questions.stem: Blocked users are kept in a `HashSet<Long> blocked`, which holds 7L. A login handler has the user id as an `int userId = 7` and checks `blocked.contains(userId)`. What happens?

options.text: It doesn't compile, since `contains` on a `HashSet<Long>` takes a `Long` parameter
options.says: contains takes an Object, so an int boxed to Integer compiles

options.text: It throws ClassCastException, since the set casts the `Integer` argument to `Long`
options.says: HashSet.contains looks the argument up with hashCode and equals and casts nothing; it just finds no match

options.text: It returns false, since the boxed `Integer` 7 is not equal to the `Long` 7
options.says: the int is boxed to Integer, and Integer.equals is false for every Long

options.text: It returns true, since the `int` 7 is widened to `long` before it is boxed
options.says: an int argument to a parameter of type Object is boxed to its own wrapper, Integer; it is never widened first

origin.section: A Wrapper Converts Only to Its Own Primitive: an Integer Is Never a Long

concepts: A compound assignment such as += casts the result back to the left-hand type, so it compiles and wraps where the plain assignment would not compile.
A cast from floating point clamps values outside the target range to MIN_VALUE or MAX_VALUE instead of keeping low bits.
Widening int or long to float, or long to double, needs no cast and rounds values beyond 24 or 53 significant bits.
